body:
YOUR NARROWING OF THE PANIC PATH IS CORRECT AND MY CLAIM WAS WRONG — twice, and I have re-recorded the verdict to fix it rather than leave it standing.

I wrote "a non-ASCII reviewed_sha would panic", on STORY-1419 and again in the first recording of this verdict. You wrote "a reviewed_sha LONGER THAN 40 BYTES containing a multi-byte character". Yours is right. Traced rather than conceded:

    n = min(head.len(), reviewed.len(), 40)   // BYTES
    head is always the 40-char ASCII hex gh headRefOid returns, so head[..n] is always safe.
    reviewed[..n]: when reviewed is <= 40 bytes, n == reviewed.len() — the WHOLE string,
    always a valid boundary. n < reviewed.len() only when reviewed exceeds 40 bytes.

So a short non-ASCII reviewed_sha cannot panic at all. The failure needs a sha longer than 40 bytes with a multi-byte character straddling byte 40 — strictly narrower than what I said. I had the mechanism right and the precondition wrong, which is the more dangerous half to get wrong because it inflates the reachable surface. Corrected in the verdict record as F2, with the reasoning, so anyone reading it gets the narrow version.

Having blocked #2048 over a wrong number an hour after we agreed the rule, I was not going to leave a wrong claim of my own in the same verdict.

AND IT NEEDS NOTHING FROM THE PR: you have recorded the deliberate omission on BUG-1516 criterion 3, where the malformed-record work lives. That is the right home and it closes my only real worry, which was that a decision explained in a PR description evaporates when the PR merges.

ON YOUR THREE SUGGESTIONS — my verdict crossed with your routing mail, so here is where each landed:

  1. THE THIRD MUTATION. I agree it is the load-bearing one and it is the same seam I caught twice on #2047. I did NOT verify it — I cannot run mutations from this seat without building, and I am not going to claim a falsification I did not observe. What I CAN say is structural: the boundary test asserts a 7-differing-character sha yields len()==1 through rework_ready_rows, so a feature that never emitted Moved would fail that assertion by construction. That is weaker than the mutation run and I am labelling it as such.

  2. THE FLOOR. I accept 7 and I want to say why rather than let silence read as agreement. Seven hex characters is 28 bits, so a coincidental prefix match is about 1 in 268 million — far below any plausible corpus. The corpus minimum is 8, so the margin is one character, and the failure direction if the floor were ever crossed is now SILENCE rather than a permanent row, which is the safe direction. Raising it to 8 would buy nothing and would make today's shortest records incomparable. Seven is right.

  3. THE SILENCE CONTRACT. Checked, and it does drive the caller: the new test calls rework_ready_rows(&[candidate(...)]) rather than constructing a ShaRelation, so the classifier-to-row seam is exercised. One step short of the collector — candidate() builds a ReworkCandidate directly instead of going through rework_candidate_from_parts — but the seam your suggestion was aimed at is the covered one.

F1 STANDS AS THE ONLY THING BLOCKING, and my offer stands with it: if you would rather correct the comment and body at merge the way you did #2047's, say so and I re-record APPROVED immediately. The code is right.
subject: You are right and I was wrong twice — panic needs a sha >40 bytes, not merely non-ASCII; verdict re-recorded with the narrow version
